# Quberi

Quberi is a multi-tenant AI knowledge base for teams. You upload documents,
members ask questions in

chat, and answers come from retrieved passages.
Retrieval is filtered by what the asking user is al

swers come from retrieved passages.
Retrieval is filtered by what the asking user is allowed to see.

**Permissions are per-document, not per-space.** Within one space, two users can
see different docum

ents. A deny rule on a document wins over any allow rule or
space role, retrieval is filtered inside

the vector index, and rules are
evaluated on every request, so a change applies to the next one.

## What it does

- **Permission-aware retrieval, per document.** Documents live in spaces, and a
space grants access

by organization, unit, position, group or individual
member, each with a role. On top of that, any s

ingle document can be shared
with someone who cannot read its space, or hidden from someone who can.

Every question is checked against both.
- **Audit log.** Sensitive actions are recorded, including

searches made by
connected outside tools.
- **Send review.** Before a question and the retrieved pas

sages go to the chat
model, you can preview them, edit them, or drop individual passages.
- **Models

.** Bring your own key, use an organization-level model, or use a
platform default. Chat uses OpenAI

-compatible endpoints. Embeddings (BGE-M3)
run inside the API and worker processes on CPU, not throu

gh a third-party API.
- **Agents.** Build knowledge assistants and connect external agents (Coze, Di

fy).
- **Sign-in and sync.** Email code, Google or Feishu login. Feishu documents can
be synced in.

- **Connected tools.** An organization admin can allow read-only search from
outside tools through O

Auth (authorization code with PKCE). It is off by
default. A plugin for DeepSeek Harness is publishe

d separately as
`dsh-quberi`. An
MCP server (listed in the
official MCP Registry as
`com.quberi/mcp`

t.
- **Member offboarding.** The organization owner can deactivate a departing
member: it ends their

web sessions, outside-tool access and Feishu sync,
removes their private model keys, and freezes th

eir personal space. See
`docs/member-offboarding.md`.
## Run it locally
Requirements: Docker with Compose, and `pnpm` if you want to work on the web app.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`QUBERI_ENCRYPTION_KEY` encrypts stored API keys and tokens. Keep it: if you lose
it, stored credent
ials cannot be read again.
Then open <http://localhost:8080>. The API listens on <http://localhost:8000>.

The stack is Postgres, Redis, Qdrant, MinIO (via the community fork
`pgsty/silo`), the API, a backgr

ound worker and the web app. See
`deploy/README.md` for details (it is written in Chinese).
### Signing in locally

Real sign-in needs SMTP, Google or Feishu to be configured in `.env`.
In a non-production environmen

t (`QUBERI_ENVIRONMENT=development`, the default in
`.env.example`), email verification codes are al

so written to the API log, so you
can try the app without a mail server:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Do not run with `QUBERI_ENVIRONMENT=development` on a machine that others can reach.
### Platform admin console

The operator's console lives at <http://localhost:8080/admin>. It is separate from
member sign-in an
d is for looking after organizations, platform models and usage.

On first boot the API creates one platform admin account (`admin`) with a random
password and writes
it **once** to the API log:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Sign in with it; the console asks you to choose your own password (12 to 128
characters) before anyt

hing else. There is no built-in default password. To pick
the first password yourself, set `QUBERI_B

OOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `.env`
before the first start; a weak value is ignored and a random one

N_PASSWORD` in `.env`
before the first start; a weak value is ignored and a random one is generated.

Because the generated password is printed to the container log, change it right
away, and treat old
logs as sensitive until you have.

`QUBERI_PLATFORM_ADMIN_TOKEN` still works as a bearer token for scripts and `curl`
against `/api/v1/

admin/*`, but the console itself only accepts a username and
password. Leave the token empty if you

do not need it. Sign-in is rate limited:
5 failed attempts on an account lock it until 15 minutes af

ter the first of those
failures, even for the right password.

The console is available in English and Simplified Chinese. Switch language at the
bottom of the sid

ebar (or below the sign-in card); it follows your browser language
the first time and remembers your

choice. Error messages from the API follow the same
language. See apps/web/src/admin/i18n/README.md
for how to add a string, a language or a message code.
## What stays on your machine

When you run the stack yourself, uploaded documents (MinIO), vectors (Qdrant),
conversations and the

audit log (Postgres) are stored on the machines you run.
Embeddings are computed locally once the m

tgres) are stored on the machines you run.
Embeddings are computed locally once the model is cached.

Questions and the retrieved passages go to whichever chat model you configure:
with a cloud API they

leave your network, and with an OpenAI-compatible model you
host yourself (for example with vLLM or

Ollama) they stay inside it. Network
access needed at run time: login codes go through your SMTP pr

ovider, Google or
Feishu sign-in talks to those services, and the first model download comes from
Hu

gle or
Feishu sign-in talks to those services, and the first model download comes from
Hugging Face.
## Security

Please do not open a public issue for a vulnerability. Use GitHub's
**Security → Report a vulnerabil

ity** to report it privately. If that is not
possible, email chaney1720@gmail.com. No response
time

possible, email chaney1720@gmail.com. No response
time is promised yet.
